findings.title: Hard DELETE relies solely on caller-supplied state guard
findings.description: The DELETE targets rows by PRIMARY key ID plus a COMPANY_STATE equality. Metadata confirms ID is a unique PRIMARY index, bounding the delete to one row; the only protection against deleting a record in an unintended state is the caller-provided COMPANY_STATE value. The mapper exposes no LIMIT or affected-row assertion.
findings.recommendation: Check the affected-row count in the service layer and fail on unexpected (0 or >1) results.

findings.title: Null COMPANY_STATE silently deletes nothing
findings.description: COMPANY_STATE is nullable in the schema. A null parameter binds as COMPANY_STATE = NULL, which never matches, silently deleting zero rows instead of surfacing an error.
findings.recommendation: Validate companyState as non-null in the service layer before invoking this mapper.

findings.title: Weakly typed Map parameter
findings.description: parameterType=java.util.Map provides no compile-time safety; a typo in a map key fails only at runtime.
findings.recommendation: Replace the Map with a typed parameter object or @Param method arguments.
